abhasa.gloss: appearance — a thing taken as that by which it shines in Consciousness, not as something standing outside it.
abhasa.name: Ābhāsa

abheda.gloss: non-duality: not "merging of two", but that there never were two. A pair to bheda.
abheda.name: Abheda

abhimana.gloss: a mistaken notion of oneself: taking the body, breath, or mind for the Self.
abhimana.name: Abhimāna

ahanta.gloss: I-consciousness — not self-conceit, but that “I” in which every experience rests. Full I-consciousness (pūrṇāhantā) is the fruit of the whole book.
ahanta.name: Ahantā

akhyati.gloss: “non-manifestation” — primordial ignorance. Kṣemarāja catches it at its word: if it does not manifest, only knowledge remains; and if it does manifest, then it is knowledge itself that manifests.
akhyati.name: Akhyāti

alangrasa.gloss: “absorption to satiety” — a pair to haṭhapāka: the object is absorbed without remainder, and no seed for a new cycle remains.
alangrasa.name: Alaṅgrāsa

ananda.gloss: Bliss — not joy about something, but that by which fullness feels itself.
ananda.name: Ānanda

anashritashiva.gloss: “Śiva supported by nothing” — the moment when the universe is not yet manifested and unity with Consciousness is not visible even to Him: an emptiness emptier than emptiness.
anashritashiva.name: Anāśritaśiva

anava.gloss: the first dirt: “I am incomplete.” Not a transgression and not ignorance of something, but the contraction of Will itself.
anava.name: Āṇava

anugraha.gloss: grace — the fifth action: that by which He reveals Himself. Here it is described as the disclosure that the thing is one with the Light.
anugraha.name: Anugraha

anuttara.gloss: “that above which there is nothing”: the Highest Reality — and the sound “a,” with which the alphabet begins and in which the universe comes to rest.
anuttara.name: Anuttara

bala.gloss: Strength — that by grasping which mantras do their work; and that, having acquired which, a person makes the universe like himself.
bala.name: Bala

bhagavati.gloss: “Blessed One,” “Mistress” — Power named as a person; in the masculine, bhagavat, “Blessed Lord.”
bhagavati.name: Bhagavatī

bhairava.gloss: the name of the Highest Lord in Trika: He who holds the universe, bears it, and draws it back in.
bhairava.name: Bhairava

bhakti.gloss: devotion. The book is written for those who have it, but lack the sharp intellect for the "Īśvarapratyabhijñā."
bhakti.name: Bhakti

bhavana.gloss: contemplative holding in the mind — not imagination, but bringing into being.
bhavana.name: Bhāvanā

bheda.gloss: separation, duality — that because of which the universe is seen as many. Its opposite is abheda, non-duality.
bheda.name: Bheda

bhoga.gloss: tasting, enjoyment. In Trika it is not opposed to liberation: the path leads to both.
bhoga.name: Bhoga

bhucari.gloss: circle of the powers of things themselves: that by which objects stand outside and apart — or, in the free one, reveal the Heart.
bhucari.name: Bhūcarī

bhumika.gloss: "role" — that which the actor plays. The eighth sutra speaks of the philosophical schools: they are all roles of the same Consciousness.
bhumika.name: Bhūmikā

bodha.gloss: understanding, wakefulness — Consciousness, taken as that which comprehends.
bodha.name: Bodha

buddhi.gloss: the discerning faculty: that which decides “this is that.”
buddhi.name: Buddhi

cakra.gloss: wheel: both a circle of deities, an assembly of powers, and a center in the body. For Kṣemarāja, more often the former.
cakra.name: Cakra

camatkara.gloss: Wonder: that taste with which Consciousness recognises itself — as one starts on recognising a long-familiar face.
camatkara.name: Camatkāra

cetana.gloss: the conscious one; cetanapada — the level of pure Consciousness, cetya — that which is conscioused by it.
cetana.name: Cetana

cit.gloss: Consciousness as such — the Light in which everything appears. citi is the same thing, named from the side of Power.
cit.name: Cit

citi.gloss: Consciousness taken as Power: the very word with which the book opens. Not “consciousness of something,” but self-luminous, free, and therefore capable of unfolding the universe from itself.
citi.name: Citi

citta.gloss: mind. The fifth sūtra says the main thing about it: the mind is not something else, but Citi itself, contracted to an object.
citta.name: Citta

deha.gloss: body. Not an obstacle: for Kṣemarāja liberation happens in the body, not after it.
deha.name: Deha

devatacakra.gloss: circle of the deities of Consciousness: the powers of the senses and the mind, taken not as instruments but as deities. Mastery over it is the fruit of the twentieth sūtra.
devatacakra.name: Devatācakra

dikcari.gloss: circle of the powers of the outer instrument — the senses, looking to the sides.
dikcari.name: Dikcarī

dvadashanta.gloss: “end of twelve” — a point twelve fingers from the body where breath ends and begins.
dvadashanta.name: Dvādaśānta

gocari.gloss: circle of the powers of the soul’s inner instrument — mind, ego, and intellect.
gocari.name: Gocarī

grahaka.gloss: “the taker” — the knower, taken as the one who grasps. A pair to grāhya, the grasped; their separation makes the universe manifold.
grahaka.name: Grāhaka

guru.gloss: teacher. The eleventh sūtra ends with the statement that without his instruction the secret course of the five actions opens to no one.
guru.name: Guru

hathapaka.gloss: “cooking by force” — a technique of Krama: to hold an object in Consciousness until it becomes equal to it, as food with fire.
hathapaka.name: Haṭhapāka

hrdaya.gloss: Heart — not an organ but a center: that to which everything converges and from which everything issues.
hrdaya.name: Hṛdaya

iccha.gloss: Will — the first of the three Powers: will, knowledge, action.
iccha.name: Icchā

ishvarata.gloss: lordship: mastery over the circle of deities of one’s own Consciousness. That very fruit with which the book ends.
ishvarata.name: Īśvaratā

jagat.gloss: world — the same universe, taken as moving and living.
jagat.name: Jagat

jivanmukti.gloss: liberation while living: freedom without leaving the body. The sixteenth sūtra is about it alone.
jivanmukti.name: Jīvanmukti

jnana.gloss: Knowledge as the Power of God — and the knowledge of an individual person, when the same Power is contracted.
jnana.name: Jñāna

kala.gloss: portion: the sheath that leaves a being with "the ability to do something" instead of omnipotence. Elsewhere — simply "portion", a part.
kala.name: Kalā

kancuka.gloss: sheath: five constrictions of omnipotence, omniscience, fullness, eternity and omnipresence — kalā, vidyā, rāga, kāla, niyati.
kancuka.name: Kañcuka

kartrtva.gloss: activity, authorship: that which you do. The limited kiñcitkartṛtva — “ability to do a little” — is omnipotence itself, compressed by the sheath.
kartrtva.name: Kartṛtva

khecari.gloss: “moving in space” — the circle of powers of the knower himself. In the bound one it hides the Heaven of Consciousness, in the free one it reveals.
khecari.name: Khecarī

krama.gloss: succession, sequence — and the name of the school from which Kṣemarāja takes kramamudrā, haṭhapāka and alaṅgrāsa.
krama.name: Krama

kriya.gloss: Action — the third Power: that by which God not only knows, but also does.
kriya.name: Kriyā

madhya.gloss: middle. For Kṣemarāja this is not a place in the body but Consciousness itself: that innermost to which everything is attached. Its unfolding is the path.
madhya.name: Madhya

mala.gloss: dirt, stain: that by which consciousness is closed off from itself. There are three of them, and in the ninth sūtra they are derived from the contraction of the three Powers.
mala.name: Mala

manas.gloss: mind as an instrument: that which assembles impressions into an image.
manas.name: Manas

maya.gloss: not illusion, but the Power of separation: that by which the One manifests itself as many, losing nothing in the process.
maya.name: Māyā

mudra.gloss: seal. bhairavīmudrā — the gaze outward while attention is inward; kramamudrā — the one that encompasses at once the external and the internal and therefore holds samādhi always.
mudra.name: Mudrā

nadi.gloss: channel through which breath flows. The central one is suṣumnā, and the seventeenth sūtra speaks of it as the middle of everything.
nadi.name: Nāḍī

pada.gloss: "place", stage, state: cetanapada — the level of pure Consciousness, pāśavapada — the state of the bound.
pada.name: Pāda

pancakrtya.gloss: fivefold action: manifestation, maintenance, withdrawal, concealment, and grace. The Lord performs them — and everyone performs the same, but does not know it; the whole book rests on knowing this authorship.
pancakrtya.name: Pañcakṛtya

parameshvara.gloss: “Highest Lord” — God taken as the master of manifestation.
parameshvara.name: Parameśvara

parishilana.gloss: exercise: to discern the same thing again and again until it becomes one’s own.
parishilana.name: Pariśīlana

pasha.gloss: fetters. They dissolve not by force, but by the recognition of one’s own nature.
pasha.name: Pāśa

pashu.gloss: “cattle” — a bound being taken as tied. Not abuse: the word speaks of bonds, not of worth. Its counterpart — pati, O Lord.
pashu.name: Paśu

pati.gloss: The Lord is the same being, but one that has recognized itself. The state pati and the state paśu differ not by nature, but by whether it is visible.
pati.name: Pati

prakasha.gloss: Light: that by which a thing is manifested at all. Without entering into it, says Kṣemarāja, nothing can be manifested.
prakasha.name: Prakāśa

prakrti.gloss: nature — the source of the material world and its three qualities.
prakrti.name: Prakṛti

pralayakala.gloss: knower of emptiness: one who has no māyic dirt, but who sleeps in dissolution.
pralayakala.name: Pralayākala

pramana.gloss: means of cognition — that by which the knower takes the knowable.
pramana.name: Pramāṇa

pramatr.gloss: the knower — the one for whom something exists. Its levels are seven, from Śiva to the bound being.
pramatr.name: Pramātṛ

prameya.gloss: the knowable — that which is taken. The same word from another side — vedya.
prameya.name: Prameya

prana.gloss: breath-life — and its ascending current in particular. The fivefold breath: prāṇa, apāna, samāna, udāna, vyāna.
prana.name: Prāṇa

pratha.gloss: spreading out: how Consciousness lays itself outward. The verb prathate — “spreads out” — and by it Kṣemarāja describes every appearance.
pratha.name: Prathā

pratyabhijna.gloss: “recognition”: not the acquisition of something new, but the acknowledgment of what has long been familiar — as one recognizes a face. The name of the books and of the entire school.
pratyabhijna.name: Pratyabhijñā

purnata.gloss: fullness — a state in which there is nothing to add and nothing to desire.
purnata.name: Pūrṇatā

puryastaka.gloss: “eightfold aggregate” — the subtle body made of eight: the five subtle elements, intellect, ego, and mind. By it a person is besieged until rooted in the One.
puryastaka.name: Puryaṣṭaka

sadashiva.gloss: the third tattva: the stage where the universe is already visible, but as a vague “this,” covered by “I.”
sadashiva.name: Sadāśiva

sakala.gloss: "with parts" — a bound being who has all three impurities: an ordinary person.
sakala.name: Sakala

samadhi.gloss: concentration. The nineteenth sūtra is about how to make it constant (nityodita) — that is, not to lose it even in the state after it, vyutthāna.
samadhi.name: Samādhi

samavesha.gloss: absorption in which the being coincides with Śiva. āveśa is the same word, entering.
samavesha.name: Samāveśa

samhara.gloss: withdrawal, dissolution — not destruction, but return into the One who manifested.
samhara.name: Saṁhāra

samsara.gloss: the cycle — not a place, but a state: to be a soul in it means not to know that the five acts are performed by you.
samsara.name: Saṁsāra

samskara.gloss: imprint: the trace of what has been experienced, which will raise it again. By them samādhi is also held in the state after samādhi.
samskara.name: Saṁskāra

samvid.gloss: Awareness — Consciousness taken as that by which any thing at all is something for someone. In Kṣemarāja this same word also stands in the place of the Highest.
samvid.name: Saṁvid

sankoca.gloss: contraction: that by which boundless Consciousness becomes this, particular. Not damage and not loss — a device of its own Freedom. The book’s main word along with citi.
sankoca.name: Saṅkoca

shakti.gloss: The Power of God, His I-Consciousness. In Kṣemarāja it is also citi: Śiva without Power manifests nothing, and there is no difference between them.
shakti.name: Śakti

shaktipata.gloss: "descent of Power": the moment when Grace touches a person. Without it, says Kṣemarāja, one's own power will not unfold.
shaktipata.name: Śaktipāta

shiva.gloss: God as the resting side of Reality — the Light of Consciousness, not different from His own Power. The book ends with the words “iti śivam”: “thus, everything is Śiva.”
shiva.name: Śiva

shunya.gloss: emptiness — a state where there is nothing knowable. Not a goal: even in it, says Kṣemarāja, traces of the mind remain.
shunya.name: Śūnya

siddhi.gloss: accomplishment. In the very first sūtra it means not a superpower, but a threefold deed: the manifestation of the world, its sustaining, and its reabsorption.
siddhi.name: Siddhi

spanda.gloss: quiver, vibration: the living tremor of Consciousness taught in the "Spanda-kārikā." Kṣemarāja refers to them most often.
spanda.name: Spanda

sphuratta.gloss: a flashing, a trembling of the Light — Consciousness taken as living, not as a motionless ground.
sphuratta.name: Sphurattā

srsti.gloss: manifestation, emission of the world — the first of the five actions.
srsti.name: Sṛṣṭi

sthiti.gloss: maintenance: that by which what is manifested is held.
sthiti.name: Sthiti

sutra.gloss: "thread" — a brief saying that does not unfold without commentary. There are twenty of them here.
sutra.name: Sūtra

svarupa.gloss: one’s own essential nature — that which a being has always been and which is hidden from it. svabhāva — the same thing in another word.
svarupa.name: Svarūpa

svatantrya.gloss: Absolute Freedom: that by which Consciousness depends on nothing — and by which it is free to bind itself.
svatantrya.name: Svātantrya

tattva.gloss: principle, "that-ness": a stage of Reality. There are thirty-six of them, from Śiva to earth; in this book they are counted in the seventh aphorism.
tattva.name: Tattva

trika.gloss: "triad" — the name of the school: Śiva, Śakti, and the bound being, taken as one.
trika.name: Trika

turya.gloss: the “fourth” state — beyond waking, dreaming sleep, and deep sleep. Beyond it is turyātīta, “that which has surpassed the fourth.”
turya.name: Turya

unmesa.gloss: “opening of the eyes”: the moment in which Consciousness opens outward. Its pair is nimeṣa, closing.
unmesa.name: Unmeṣa

upadesha.gloss: instruction: the oral indication of the teacher, not knowledge gleaned from reading.
upadesha.name: Upadeśa

upaya.gloss: means. The easy means (sukhopāya) is what this book boasts of: a path requiring neither breath retention nor postures.
upaya.name: Upāya

vameshvari.gloss: “The Lady who pours forth” — the Power that emits the universe; she also leads by the reverse course out of the cycle. Her four circles are khecarī, gocarī, dikcarī, bhūcarī.
vameshvari.name: Vāmeśvarī

vidya.gloss: knowledge — and that tattva, śuddhavidyā, where "I" and "this" still hold together; below māyā it becomes the narrow knowledge of a single person.
vidya.name: Vidyā

vijnanakala.gloss: pure Consciousness without action: it retains only the first impurity. Above māyā and below Pure Vidyā.
vijnanakala.name: Vijñānākala

vikalpa.gloss: thought, a discriminating notion: “this is not that.” avikalpa — a state where they are absent, and the first of the means of the eighteenth sūtra leads there.
vikalpa.name: Vikalpa

vikasa.gloss: unfolding — the pair to contraction. Liberation here is described precisely as the unfolding of the middle, not as arrival somewhere else.
vikasa.name: Vikāsa

vilaya.gloss: concealment: the fourth action, by which God hides Himself from Himself. Without it there would be no grace either.
vilaya.name: Vilaya

vimarsha.gloss: the Light’s response to itself — that by which the Light knows that it is. The pair to prakāśa, and they are not two.
vimarsha.name: Vimarśa

vishranti.gloss: repose — not rest after work, but that into which every movement comes and in which it holds. Utpaladeva says: the repose of all experience in oneself is what is called “I.”
vishranti.name: Viśrānti

vishva.gloss: universe — everything from Sadāśiva to the earth element. For Kṣemarāja it is not made of something, but unfolded on the very canvas of Consciousness.
vishva.name: Viśva

vyamohitata.gloss: being led astray by one’s own powers. The twelfth sūtra says that this is what it means to be a soul in the cycle: not sin and not punishment, but non-recognition.
vyamohitata.name: Vyāmohitatā
